findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean:173 `lemma Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul (n : ℤ) (b : M) : (n : R) • b = n • b`; Mathlib/Algebra/Star/Module.lean:48 `theorem star_intCast_smul ... (n : ℤ) (x : M) : star ((n : R) • x) = ...`; Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean:200 `map_intCast_smul`. Statements at Exp.lean:91,100,138 all read `exp ((t : ℚ) • x)`.
findings.fix: Either state the hypothesis/conclusion with the genuine `ℤ`-action `(t : ℤ) • x` (equal by `Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul`, which the proof at line 94 already invokes), keeping the names; or rename to `exp_intCast_smul_eq_sum_zsmul_dividedPower` / `exp_intCast_smul_mem` / `exp_intCast_smul_conj_mem`. Note only the *second* `zsmul` in the expansion lemma is genuine (`t ^ i • dividedPower i x`, `t ^ i : ℤ`).
findings.issue: `exp_zsmul_eq_sum_zsmul_dividedPower`, `exp_zsmul_mem` (line 98) and `exp_zsmul_conj_mem` (line 136) all state `exp ((t : ℚ) • x)`, an `Int.cast` scalar in the ℚ-action, not a `ℤ`-smul. Mathlib names `((n : R) • x)` with `intCast_smul` and reserves `zsmul` for `n • x` with `n : ℤ`. A user rewriting a goal `exp ((t : ℤ) • x) ∈ S` with `exp_zsmul_mem` will fail to match.

findings.evidence: Exp.lean:179 `theorem exp_ad_apply ... : exp (LieAlgebra.ad ℚ A a) b = ...` versus Exp.lean:187 `exp a * b = exp (LieAlgebra.ad ℚ A a) b * exp a`.
findings.issue: `exp_mul_eq_exp_ad_mul` describes the RHS `exp (ad ℚ A a) b * exp a` as `exp_ad_mul`, which reads as the product `exp (ad a) * …`; the term is an application of the endomorphism `exp (ad a)` to `b`. The adjacent lemma at line 179 spells exactly this term `exp_ad_apply`.

summary: Six declarations use `zsmul` for what is an `Int.cast` rational scalar `((t : ℤ) : ℚ) • x`, which Mathlib names `intCast_smul`; two further names are inconsistent with their own adjacent declarations. No notation is introduced.
